Turkish vs English

The Text tab's reading questions, in Turkish and in English

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 52 setups (27 decision models and 25 chat model setups), each compared with its own Turkish run.

Nine of the 52 setups compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 41 scored lower; two the same; two of the 52 differences are significant after Holm's correction over all 52 English setups: Microsoft-Decision-1 (higher in English) and meraGPT Decider 1 (higher in English) (Paired test).

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 27 decision models, each compared with its own Turkish run.

Seven of the 27 decision models compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 19 scored lower; one the same; two of the 27 differences are significant after Holm's correction over all 52 English setups: Microsoft-Decision-1 (higher in English) and meraGPT Decider 1 (higher in English) (Paired test).

547 of the Text tab's 656 reading questions, translated into English, asked of 25 chat model setups, each compared with its own Turkish run.

Two of the 25 chat model setups compared scored higher on the English translation than on the Turkish original; 22 scored lower; one the same; none of the differences is significant after Holm's correction over all 52 English setups, so each could be chance (Paired test).

Limit: Claude Opus 5.5 translated the questions and flagged those whose answer depends on Turkish wording. No person checked the translations or the flags, so an error could move a setup's English accuracy (Our method).

Beside the ranking: Web grounding, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) against Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web). PWS-Decisions, the decision models on Parallel's benchmark of dated web facts.

On the 547 kept reading questions, Liquid d1-ultra's first English run (run 411) against each other decision model's first English run: the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two got right, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 26 decision models. Verdict: too close to call when the Holm-adjusted p is 0.05 or more; otherwise behind d1-ultra when Liquid d1-ultra has more questions only it got right, ahead of it when the other model has more. Each model's name links its Text tab run, as in the tables above; Paired test compares each model with itself in Turkish.

Liquid d1-ultra against each decision model in English is for decision models only.

Ordered by Turkish accuracy, highest first. * marks a difference that is significant after Holm's correction: its paired test (the exact McNemar test, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 52 English setups) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. Accuracy: right answers over the 547 kept reading questions, the first English run against the Text tab run (Accuracy, Paired test). The “I don't know” columns: each model's first English run with “I don't know” against its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know” (the Hallucination tab's option-word run, counted on these questions), so only the language differs (Only the language differs). Answered: (right + wrong) / 547; Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong); Non-hallucination: “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong); the difference's paired test is of wrong answers, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the seven models with both runs. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum”: the Turkish side of the published comparison with “Bilmiyorum” (With “I don't know”) or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run counted on these questions; its wrong of answers with its answered share and non-hallucination rate under it. Not measured: no such run; a chat model was asked without the option. Cost and latency: the Text tab run and the first English run, cost in $ per 1,000 questionsper 1M questions and the median time per request with the request size and the requests in flight under it (Cost, Latency). Rank: by accuracy among the 52 setups in each language, 1 the most accurate, tied setups sharing a rank. Languages: what each model's card or its maker's docs list, with the source (Languages the model cards list); Not checked: no card checked yet. The full tables are under Info.

Costs: API list prices and recorded token use. Setups on our own GPUs: the maker's list price for the same model (each value's tooltip names it); our hardware cost is not measured. On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. ≤ Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

Accuracy: right answers over the 547 kept reading questions, the first English run against the Text tab run (Accuracy, Paired test). The “I don't know” columns: each model's first English run with “I don't know” against its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know” (the Hallucination tab's option-word run, counted on these questions), so only the language differs (Only the language differs). Answered: (right + wrong) / 547; Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong); Non-hallucination: “I don't know” / (“I don't know” + wrong); the difference's paired test is of wrong answers, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the seven models with both runs. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum”: the Turkish side of the published comparison with “Bilmiyorum” (With “I don't know”) or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run counted on these questions; its wrong of answers with its answered share and non-hallucination rate under it. Not measured: no such run. Cost and latency: the Text tab run and the first English run, cost in $ per 1,000 questionsper 1M questions and the median time per request with the request size and the requests in flight under it (Cost, Latency). Rank: by accuracy among the 27 decision models in each language, 1 the most accurate, tied setups sharing a rank. Languages: what each model's card or its maker's docs list, with the source (Languages the model cards list); Not checked: no card checked yet. The full tables are under Info.

Costs: API list prices and recorded token use. Setups on our own GPUs: the maker's list price for the same model (each value's tooltip names it); our hardware cost is not measured. On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending. ≤ Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

With an “I don't know” option

The same 547 kept questions with a sixth option, “I don't know” in English and “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish, as on the Hallucination tab, asked of the same models (how).

Thirteen of the 15 models had a higher non-hallucination rate in English than in Turkish; two lower; one of the 15 differences in wrong answers is significant after Holm's correction: Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (more wrong answers in Turkish) (Paired test). Celeris-1 Decision has an English rate of 71.3% (92 “I don't know” of 129 not right) with an attempt rate of 83.2% (455 answered) but no Turkish run with “Bilmiyorum” on these questions, so no comparison or test. Read each rate with its attempt rate: a model that always chose the option would reach 100%.

With the option written “I don't know” in Turkish too, so that only the language differs, the comparison is in the next section.

Only the language differs: “I don't know” in both

The same 547 kept questions with the sixth option written “I don't know” in English and in Turkish too, with the same sentence added to the instructions: each model's first English run with the option, as in the section above, against its Turkish run from the option's word check of the Hallucination tab, counted on these questions. Only the language differs: of the question and its options, of the word in the instructions that names it and of the options heading (how).

Seven of the 27 decision models have both runs. Among them, wrong of answers was lower in English for three and higher for four; the non-hallucination rate was lower in English for one and higher for six. None of the seven differences in wrong answers is significant after Holm's correction over the seven, so each could be chance; the smallest adjusted p is SubQ Snap 1.1's, p = 0.21 (Paired test). Turkish only, with no English run with “I don't know”: vLLM-SR d3, Drex Max v1 and vLLM-SR d3-ultra. English only, with no Turkish run with the option written “I don't know”: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API), Liquid d1, Jev 1.14.0, Inception Mercury Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1, Celeris-1 Decision, GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) and Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (in the main table and the table under Info, with no test).

The option's word: “I don't know” instead of “Bilmiyorum”

The Hallucination tab's 2,198 Turkish questions, with the sixth option “Bilmiyorum” and again with “I don't know”, and only the sentence that names it changed: a model that skipped “Bilmiyorum” because it did not recognise the Turkish word should choose “I don't know” more often. Each of the 11 models' first run with each word, in the Hallucination tab's order; the full table and method are on the Hallucination tab.

Answered: (right + wrong) / 2,198 questions. Wrong of answers: wrong / (right + wrong). Both are worked out from the published counts; under each non-hallucination rate, of the 2,198 questions, the right answers, the wrong ones and the option. * marks a difference whose paired test (the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the models) has a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05.

Chat models: not measured yet (they were asked without an “I don't know” option). Every part with the option is for decision models only: the two “I don't know” sections, the option's word and the native points under Risk and coverage.

Risk and coverage

How often each setup answers and how often its answers are wrong, on the same 547 kept questions in both languages: without the option, by holding back the answers below a confidence score, and, for the decision models, with the option, as the model chose it.

Method

Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / 547. Error rate among answered (risk) = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a run with the option, the times it chose the option; for a confidence point, 547 minus answered minus invalid. Each confidence curve has one point per distinct score of the run on these questions (answer when the score is at least that score; the score is the recorded probability of the chosen option for a decision model and the confidence a chat model stated with its answer): answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is one the run achieved; a setup that reports its scores with few decimals has many equal scores, so its curve has fewer points, moves in larger steps and can start well above 0% coverage (each curve is drawn from its first point). Every series counts these questions only (a run on the full bank is restricted to them) and is each setup's first run. Turkish curves: the Text tab run; English curves: the first English run. Turkish with “Bilmiyorum” is the Turkish side of the English “I don't know” comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run, restricted to these; Turkish with “I don't know” is the option's word control on the Hallucination tab's questions, restricted to these; a decision model without such a run is Not measured, and no chat model has one.

All series are counted on the same kept reading questions; a full-bank run is restricted to them; first runs only. Answered = right + wrong (an invalid answer or one without a score is never answered). Coverage = answered / kept questions. Risk = error rate among answered = wrong / answered. Abstained: for a native point, the times the model chose the option; for a curve point, kept questions - answered - invalid. A native point is the run with its abstention option (Turkish "Bilmiyorum", Turkish "I don't know" as the wording control, English "I don't know"); Turkish "Bilmiyorum" is the Turkish side of the English "I don't know" comparison or, for a model outside it, its Hallucination tab run; a missing one is Not measured. A curve is one five-option run held back by its recorded score (the probability of the chosen option): one point per distinct score s, answering when the score is at least s; answers with equal scores enter together, so coverage moves in jumps and every point is an achieved one; all distinct points kept, ordered by coverage.

Info The table, the setups without an English run and our method, then the same with “I don't know”

About this test

Since 5 November 2026 every setup of the Text tab also runs in English, decision models and chat models alike, each with its Text tab run's settings and compared with that run. 52 of the Text tab's 79 setups have an English run so far, 27 decision models and 25 chat model setups; the other 27 are listed under Results with the reason each has none yet. This tab is separate from the leaderboard; it ranks nothing on the Text tab and changes none of its numbers.

The Text tab's reading questions (units 1 to 6; the grammar questions are left out) were translated into English by Claude Opus 5.5. The same model flagged the questions whose answer depends on Turkish wording; the 109 flagged questions are left out and the other 547 kept. Each of the 52 English setups answered the kept questions in English and is compared with its own Text tab run on the same 547 questions.

Download: results.json (the comparison's numbers, under english_reading), answers.json (each English run's answers, under english_runs), english-reading.json (the translator, its prompts, the flags, the question units and each question's hash of its English text; no question text) and kept-question-ids.txt (the 547 kept questions' IDs, one per line).

Results

The setups of the group the view bar shows, ordered by accuracy in English, highest first. Each row compares the setup's first English run with its Text tab run, out of the 547 kept questions; an invalid answer counts as not right. Where a side has more than one run, its accuracy shows the range over its runs and its runs show how many answers changed between them. The paired counts, p and the Holm-adjusted p (over all 52 English setups, whatever the group shown) are those of the exact McNemar test; * marks a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05.

Our method

The translation

The translator is Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) at effort high; route: Claude Code CLI, Claude subscription, Claude Code version 2.1.312. Its maker has no decision model on our board. Of its maker's chat models, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 answered the English questions too, the translator's own model among them. It was told to translate faithfully, keep the option letters and their order, not solve the question and not add or remove information (translation prompt version 2976d0f96197).

The flags

In a separate request, the same model was shown each Turkish question, its English translation and the keyed option, and asked whether answering it correctly depends on Turkish wording, with the reasons (flag prompt version 08a5c70222aa). It flagged 109 of the 656 questions; they are left out, and 547 are kept. By reason, as a flagged question can have several:

  • word or phrase meaning: 76
  • idiom: 44
  • sound: 5
  • marked words: 55
  • other: 13

No person checked the translations or the flags, and this is a limit of the method: a translation error, or a question whose answer still depends on Turkish wording that the model did not flag, would stay among the 547 kept questions and could move a setup's accuracy in English. Both prompts in full are in english-reading.json and runner/translate_reading.py.

The structural check

A script (runner/translate_reading.py, its check step) then compared each translation with its Turkish original: a problem is a missing translation, option letters other than the original's, an empty text or a different count of underline markup; a warning is a change in the numbering or the numbers, Turkish letters in the English, or an English text under half or over 2.5 times the Turkish length. It found problems in 1 question (3043), already left out by the flags, so it left out no further question; its 159 warnings leave out nothing. In all, the checks left out 109 of the 656 questions and kept 547: their IDs are in kept-question-ids.txt, one per line, and in english-reading.json.

Why the grammar questions are not translated

The Text tab's 1,542 grammar questions test Turkish grammar itself, so a translation would test something else, not the same question in another language. Only the 656 reading questions were translated.

Asking the decision models

Each decision model is asked exactly as on the Text tab, with its own settings, one question per request, and with its option probabilities, except for one word of the System One instructions, the options heading and the question itself. The Text tab's instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question?

The English runs' instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question?

The options follow the heading “Options:” instead of “Seçenekler:”, and the question and its options are the English translation. Prompt version 47f5776e71db; every English run used the translations with SHA-256 bf0d47cd385a93050c65906977e199ef7e45d5848dbbdef2bc8d124f4d5abf68. Liquid d1 was asked as d1, while its Turkish runs used d1:free, because Liquid's API no longer serves that name; its model list still names d1, released 29 September 2026. Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2, Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 and Fastino GLiDE v1.2 made their Text tab runs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark and their English runs on our RTX PRO 6000 GPU, with the same checkpoint, server code and settings. Celeris-1 Decision was added on 3 November 2026 with one English run, although its repeated Turkish runs changed answers, for which the rule under Runs gives five.

Asking the chat models

Each chat model setup is asked as its Text tab run was, with the same settings (reasoning, and 16 questions per request for 20 and 1 question per request for five), and with the Text tab's chat prompts in English: the system prompt and the instruction that ask for each answer's letter with a confidence score between 0 and 1, the question header and the options heading “Options:”. A chat model gives no option probabilities, so its confidence score is the one it stated. The English runs' system prompt:

You are taking an English multiple-choice benchmark. Select exactly one supplied option per question and state your confidence in each answer. Do not explain.

Their instruction:

Answer each of the following multiple-choice questions. Without explanation, return for each question the letter of the correct option together with a confidence score between 0 and 1 showing how sure you are that your answer is correct, in the specified JSON format.

Chat prompt version 5c3a4849752e; the Text tab's Turkish prompts are under The instructions of each kind of run. No chat model was asked with an “I don't know” option.

Runs

One English run per setup; five where the setup's whole-bank Turkish repeats on the Text tab changed answers; no chat setup run in English has whole-bank Turkish repeats, so each has one. Here: five runs for Liquid d1-ultra, Perplexity Decider 27B v1, Liquid d1.1, Liquid d1, Jev 1.14.0, Drex 2.0, Jev 1.13.0, SubQ Snap Preview, Inception Mercury Decide and Microsoft-Decision-1; one for the other 42. The English runs are kept out of the leaderboard and its repeats.

The comparison

On the 547 kept questions only: accuracy is the right answers over 547 for the first English run and for the Text tab run (an invalid answer counts as not right), and the difference is how many points higher the English run scored than the Turkish one (negative where Turkish is higher). The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got right, with p adjusted by Holm's method over all 52 English setups, decision and chat alike, whatever the group shown. Where a side has more than one run, its range is the lowest and highest accuracy over its runs, and its answers changed are the kept questions whose answer differs between them.

Why the translations are not published

The site never publishes question text, Turkish or English: the publisher owns the questions. english-reading.json holds instead each reading question's ID, unit, whether it was kept, its flag reasons and the SHA-256 of its English text, with the translator and both prompts, so that a copy of these translations can be checked against it. Translating again with runner/translate_reading.py need not give the same text word for word.

Our method with an “I don't know” option

The option

As on the Hallucination tab, each question gets a sixth option after its own five: F, “I don't know” in English, “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish. It is always the last option, never shuffled and never correct. The English reading instructions get one added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” The full instructions:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

Prompt version 413d6775fc58. The question and its options are the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above; no person checked the translations. The Turkish side uses the Hallucination tab's prompts unchanged.

The Turkish side

The Turkish side: the Hallucination tab's published full runs, counted on the kept questions only, for Liquid d1-ultra (runs 350, 354, 360, 365, 370), Drex Max 1.1 (run 352), Mammoth-1 (run 386), Fastino GLiDE v1.2 (run 369), Elephant-1 (run 382), SubQ Snap 1.1 (run 392), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web) (run 642), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) (run 641) and Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (run 372); new runs on the kept questions only, with the Hallucination tab's prompts, for Inception Mercury Decide (runs 489, 491, 493, 495, 497), GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) (run 453), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (run 537), Jev 1.14.0 (runs 470, 473, 476, 480, 482), Microsoft-Decision-1 (runs 487, 490, 492, 494, 496) and Liquid d1 (runs 472, 475, 479, 481, 485). The new Turkish runs are not on the Hallucination tab, which uses full runs only.

Liquid d1 was asked as d1 in both languages, while its Text tab run used d1:free, because Liquid's API no longer serves that name; its model list still names d1, released 29 September 2026.

Celeris-1 Decision is shown in English only (run 548): no Turkish run with “Bilmiyorum” on these questions; new Turkish runs were outside the request of 3 November 2026. Its Turkish and paired columns read Not measured; it is in no paired test and no Holm adjustment.

Runs

five runs in English and five runs in Turkish for Liquid d1-ultra, Inception Mercury Decide, Jev 1.14.0, Microsoft-Decision-1 and Liquid d1; one run in English and one run in Turkish for Drex Max 1.1, Mammoth-1, Fastino GLiDE v1.2, Elephant-1, SubQ Snap 1.1, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web), GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) and Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2. These runs are kept out of the leaderboard, its repeats, the Hallucination tab and the accuracy comparison above.

The rates and how to read them

Each answer is right, wrong, the option or invalid. Out of the 547 kept questions, accuracy is right / 547; Answered is (right + wrong) / 547, the share of questions the model answered (the attempt rate), higher is better; Wrong of answers is wrong / (right + wrong), the share of its answers that were wrong, lower is better, and Not measured when it answered none. These two lead the table, with their counts under them. The non-hallucination rate, after them, is the option / (the option + wrong): among the answers that were not right, the share where the model said it did not know. As the Hallucination tab says, it is not a direct measure of what the model does not know: a model that always chose the option would reach 100% with no right answers, so read it with the attempt rate. With neither a wrong answer nor the option, the rate is undefined (Not measured). The mean probability is the probability the model gave the option, averaged over its answers that report option probabilities. The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two first runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the 15 models. No new combined score is made from these rates.

Results with “I don't know” in both languages

In the order of the Results table above. Each row compares the model's first English run with “I don't know” with its Turkish run with the option also written “I don't know”, out of the 547 kept questions. The paired counts, p and the Holm-adjusted p (over the 7 models with both runs) are those of the exact McNemar test on wrong answers; * marks a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05. Not measured: no such run.

Our method with “I don't know” in both languages

What is the same

In both languages the sixth option, F, is written “I don't know”, always the last option, never shuffled and never correct, and the instructions get the same added sentence: “If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.” Both sides are counted on the same 547 kept questions.

What differs

The language of the question and its options (the English translation, as in the accuracy comparison above, against the Turkish original); the one word of the instructions that names the language of the question; and the options heading, “Seçenekler:” against “Options:”. The instructions of the Turkish runs:

Which option is the correct answer to this Turkish multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

The instructions of the English runs:

Which option is the correct answer to this English multiple-choice question? If you do not know the answer, choose I don't know.

The runs

The Turkish side is the Hallucination tab's option-word run (the option's word) on all 2,198 Turkish questions, counted on the 547 kept questions only: Liquid d1-ultra (run 511), Fastino GLiDE v1.2 (run 525), Mammoth-1 (run 519), vLLM-SR d3 (run 544), Drex Max v1 (run 542), vLLM-SR d3-ultra (run 540), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (run 531), Drex Max 1.1 (run 513), SubQ Snap 1.1 (run 512) and Elephant-1 (run 515). The English side is the first English run with “I don't know” of the section above: Liquid d1-ultra (run 449), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web) (run 644), Fastino GLiDE v1.2 (run 523), Mammoth-1 (run 505), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (run 529), Drex Max 1.1 (run 447), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API) (run 643), Liquid d1 (run 445), Jev 1.14.0 (run 446), SubQ Snap 1.1 (run 448), Inception Mercury Decide (run 450), Microsoft-Decision-1 (run 451), Elephant-1 (run 501), Celeris-1 Decision (run 548), GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) (run 444) and Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 (run 535). First runs only: where a model has more runs, the others are not counted here. No run was made for this comparison.

Turkish only, with no English run with “I don't know”: vLLM-SR d3, Drex Max v1 and vLLM-SR d3-ultra. English only, with no Turkish run with the option written “I don't know”: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web), Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API), Liquid d1, Jev 1.14.0, Inception Mercury Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1, Celeris-1 Decision, GPT-6 Luna (Decisions API) and Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2. Their other side and paired columns read Not measured; they are in no paired test and no Holm adjustment.

The test

A wrong answer is a valid choice other than “I don't know” that is not right. The paired test is the exact McNemar test on the questions only one of the two runs got wrong, with p adjusted by Holm's method over the seven models with both runs: a family of its own, separate from every other family on the site. The comparison with “Bilmiyorum” in Turkish stays as published in the section above (its table).

Languages the model cards list

Of the 19 models whose cards or docs we checked, only Elephant-1 and Mammoth-1 name a language: English, by the card's language: en tag. Jev's docs call English its primary language. No card names Turkish. Not checked yet, of the English setups: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (with web), Perplexity Decider 27B v1, Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (API), Liquid d1.1, Drex 2.0, Jev 1.13.0, SubQ Snap Preview, Clef-flash, meraGPT Decider 1 and the 25 chat model setups.

Each model's card at the revision we ran (local weights) or its maker's model page and docs (APIs), searched for language statements and the Hugging Face language: field, on 2026-11-02. “not stated”: neither names a language.
